properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of Greenwood County, South Carolina

* WHEN...Until 130 AM EDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 729 PM EDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicate an axis of training thunderstorms are impacting
Greenwood County from Bradley to Promised Land to the City of
Greenwood to Coronaca.  These storms are producing torrential
rainfall rates of 2-4" per hour, and rain accumulations of
1-2" are rapidly developing.  Given saturated topsoils,
excessive runoff is occurring and rapid rises are imminent on
Armstrong Branch, Coronaca Creek, Sample Branch, Rocky Creek,
and Brightmans Creek, as well as adjacent smaller drainages
and tributaries.  Some streams will exceed bankfull and cause
nuisance to Minor flooding of adjacent low-lying areas.
Flood-prone areas of the City of Greenwood are likely to be
impacted.

- If storm-total rainfall amounts exceed 3-4 inches over the
next 60 minutes, more significant flooding may develop and a
Flash Flood Warning may be issued.  Caution is advised near
any stream or other  vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground
immediately if streams start to rise.  Please have a plan in
place should flash flooding develop and do not hesitate to
act.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Greenwood, Promised Land, Bradley and Coronaca.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 644 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicates a cluster of
thunderstorms have developed over Laurens County, primarily
from Waterloo to Laurens to Ora within the Little River and
Duncan Creek headwaters.  These cells are producing
torrential rainfall rates of 3-4" per hour, and accumulations
of 1-2" are rapidly developing.  Given saturated topsoils,
excessive runoff is imminent and rapid rises on the Little
River, Duncan Creek, Cane Creek, and associated tributaries
is expected.  Some streams may exceed bankfull and cause
flooding of adjacent low-lying areas.

Areas of greatest concern include along Duncan Creek near SC
49 and SC 308, flood-prone areas of the City of Laurens,
including along the Little River near Gordon St and Little
River Park, and Burnt Mill Creek near Pinehaven St Extension,
Powers Rd, and SC 127.

- If storm-total rainfall amounts exceed 3-4 inches over the
next 1-2 hours, more significant flooding may develop and a
Flash Flood Warning may be issued.  Caution is advised near
any stream or other vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground
immediately if streams start to rise.  Please have a plan in
place should flash flooding develop and do not hesitate to
act.

Laurens, Clinton, Cross Hill, Waterloo, Mountville and Ora.

upstream. There are reports that Kwiguk Pass is jamming up at
the mouth and that water will begin backing up into Emmonak.

conjunction with this ice run. Residents should take
precautions now and continue to monitor the situation
closely.
